text:
sam: Prod alert — multiple customers getting 504/timeout errors on hosted API. SLOs show p50 stable, p95 spiking; some requests hitting gateway deadline. Looks like requests are building up behind the continuous batcher during a small-request spike.

maya: Copy. Any reproducible pattern? which model/route is most affected?

sam: Top affected route: /v1/generate (lighter model). Metrics show queue_length jumped from ~200 -> 12,400 over ~8m, batcher_active_batches=350, dequeue rate stalled. Sample logs: 

```log
[2026-03-17T14:03:12Z] gateway: accept req id=abc123 size=64
[2026-03-17T14:03:12Z] batcher: enqueued id=abc123 queue_len=12400
[2026-03-17T14:03:42Z] gateway: deadline exceeded req id=abc123 status=504
[2026-03-17T14:04:00Z] queue: eviction triggered tenant=foodly reason=depth_limit
```

sam: Quick repro we ran from load infra (produces same pileup):

```bash
for i in {1..5000}; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"input":"hi"}' &
done; wait
```

ajay: Oncall here. Observed behavior is consistent with continuous-batcher dequeue loop stalling when a small-request flood coincides with a slow backend GPU in pool A, causing KV cache hot-switch thrash. Did we push the quantization/kernel update to pool A today?

maya: Yes — that canary reached pool A ~03:30 UTC (5% rollout).

ajay: Immediate mitigations I'm going to apply: 1) route traffic off pool A to fallback pool B, 2) temporarily raise per-tenant queue depth threshold for 10m, 3) enable aggressive prefix-cache bypass for tiny payloads. Applying 1+2 now.

ingest-bot: deploy: rollout (fallback-routing) started by ajay. changelist 7f3a2

ajay: Routing shifted to pool B and threshold raised. Queue length drained to ~300 over ~4m, 504s dropped to near-zero. Monitoring.

elena: Noted. I'll notify affected customers with timeline + mitigation. Sam, please attach repro steps & logs to the incident ticket and follow support playbook.

sam: Adding to ticket. Root-cause hypothesis: kernel/quant update + small-request storm -> batcher backlog + per-tenant depth triggering evictions/timeouts. Proposed follow-ups: revert canary in pool A, add rollout guardrails (rate-limited canary, fail-open routing), improve KV cache warmup probe and add early-bypass for tiny inputs.

maya: Agree. I'll open PR for rollout guardrails and add a preflight check to the canary job.

ajay: We'll keep this P1 until the postmortem and fixes land. Check back in 1h.

sam: Thanks all — will close once postmortem and customer comms are posted.
